cuts.item: Layoffs and program eliminations to fit fire fourth shift into a core-services override
cuts.who: the vice chair of the select board

statements.statement: Federal entitlement grants to the schools were cut by about $123,000 (chair said about $100,000, corrected from the floor).
statements.who: the chair of the school committee

statements.statement: A member proposed an override of $3 million, saying it would give the schools close to or more than half.
A $3 million override would add $636 per year ($63627 as heard) to the average single-family bill of $517,296; current FY26 bill $7,444; does not include FY27 2.5%.
Property tax is the largest revenue source in the funding line, at $36.3 million.
The assessors voted a $260,000 overlay account.
Revenue estimates were adjusted by about $175,000: $100,000 on investment income and $75,000 on motor vehicle excise tax.
The school committee has stuck to its restoration budget at 1.9 (million) and said it could have asked for $4 million.
A $4 million override was cited as costing $800 a year for the average household (disputed in discussion).
Health insurance assumed to rise 9% a year.
Local receipts came in about $1.6 million extra this past year.
Straw poll, non-binding: everyone favored putting an override on the ballot; 7 favored one override number, 5 (6 with one more) favored two.
Ballot question language and number must reach the town clerk by April 11; the motion number must match the ballot question.

warnings.prediction: An override failing would be devastating to schools, fire and everything, as in 2012.
Fire department may not be able to show up, one less school resource officer, possibly no high school sports.
A balanced cut budget will be incredibly difficult and decimate the school system.

warnings.condition: if only bare-bones level services is funded
warnings.prediction: The town will be back next year doing the same thing, with 9% health insurance increases.

warnings.condition: if the override only funds level services
warnings.prediction: A level services override will not pass; parents won't vote for the status quo.
warnings.who: the chair of the school committee

warnings.prediction: Financial catastrophe is coming over the next two years.
warnings.who: the chair of the school committee

warnings.condition: if a core-services tier is chosen
warnings.prediction: Core-services option would require drastic cuts including potential layoffs.
warnings.who: the vice chair of the select board

warnings.condition: if one large number is put forward and fails
warnings.prediction: Going to one number could mean losing the override and, as in 2012, program damage like band shrinking.

warnings.condition: if only a level/core services budget goes forward
warnings.prediction: A member will do no campaigning for a level or core services budget.
